workingTitle: Double Fine Returns To Kickstarter Post-Xbox, Announces New Game Jam

secondary.title: Double Fine Returns To Kickstarter Post-Xbox, Announces New Game Jam
"Buying any of our games helps support the studio": Psychonauts studio Double Fine are the latest former Xbox-owned studio to get the rights to their games back
Double Fine confirms it owns all its games' IP and publishing rights after Xbox split
Double Fine Owns IP and Publishing Rights for All of Its Games Following Xbox Split, Psychonauts Studio Confirms
The newly independent Psychonauts dev now earns all the revenue when you buy games it made under Xbox: 'Buying any of our games helps support the studio'
Psychonauts Dev Double Fine Will Let You Decide What Game It Makes Next

Schafer also revealed Double Fine's next move will be to revive its Amnesia Fortnight game jam as a Kickstarter campaign, letting backers vote on which prototype becomes the studio's next full project.

facts.context:
Double Fine itself laid off roughly a quarter of its 90-person team as part of the transition, saying at the time that the cuts were needed to reach "a size that we can sustain."

Compulsion Games, the We Happy Few and South of Midnight studio also cut loose from Xbox in the same restructuring, has similarly confirmed it retains ownership of its IP.

He went on, explaining, "it just takes a while for it to all process." The headline, though, is that "when people buy our games, it supports the studio."

"If you're curious, buying any of our games helps support the studio," he repeated.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma promised that Double Fine, as well as South of Midnight developer Compulsion Games, would retain their IP, catalog, and a "runway for their next games" when they were listed as part of a grand restructuring plan early last month.

Double Fine's transition back into an independent studio was almost immediately followed by layoffs affecting 25% of its team.

Later this month, the studio will start a Kickstarter campaign based around its annual Amnesia Fortnight game jam, which is the same game jam where some of its previous games, like Costume Quest and Stacking, were born.

singleSourced.context: Schafer said the Kickstarter campaign and the revenue from its games will help the studio "have as much runway as possible" as it works on pitching other projects to publishers.
